note: Cut-pattern library (data). cuts/cutgen.py turns a BPM + a pattern into frame-exact cut points. Beat positions are in beats from the start of each cycle (4/4 assumed: 1 bar = 4 beats). Numbers are house starting values [H] from docs/research/edit.md sections 2.3, 2.5, 3.3, 6.1, 7.2 and docs/research/sound.md 4.10 / bundle.short_film: tune by retention data, never treat as platform facts.

every_beat.use: drop / chorus montage, 120-150 BPM gives 0.4-0.5 s shots

every_bar.use: verses, product holds, talking-head B-roll on music

every_2bars.use: intros, emotional holds, short film on score

eighths.use: 1-2 bar burst only (stutter montage); never sustained (flash safety for flashes)

push_and.use: anticipation: the cut before the bar line lands early, pulls into the next bar

tresillo_332.use: 3+3+2 eighths: groove, Afro-Latin and pop hooks

downbeat_hits.use: 4-bar phrase with a turnaround: two quick cuts lead into the next phrase

build_accelerate.then: hero cut on the next downbeat (riser ends there: sfx/riser/* length = whole bars)

drop_doubletime.use: chorus or drop after a build

hook_3s.use: short-form hook: >= 3 visual states in the first 5 s (ABCD R3)

breath_out.use: decelerate into an end card (decelerate before a CTA)

J.use: next scene's audio starts before its picture: anticipation, scene bridges, interviews

L.use: previous audio lingers over new picture: reaction shots, dialogue overlap

film_J.use: short-film scene change: sound leads the cut (docs/research/sound.md bundle.short_film)

broll_lead.use: talking-head B-roll: the PICTURE leads the VO line by 150 ms (micro J, inverted)

autocut.analysis_by: talking-head-recut / video-use skills (reuse; this file only holds the numbers)

reframe_alternate.use: disguise jump cuts: every jump cut changes framing, anchored on the eyes

punch_in.use: key claims and predictable dips; max 1 per 4 s

beat_hold.use: hold the face 400-600 ms after a punchline, then cut

cut_tick.use: optional jump-cut tick so cuts are not sterile

smash.use: comedy, shock, irony, problem-to-solved snap, mime-style punchline; the silence before is what sells it

interruptOpen.bed: the music stops on the stop frame (tape stop, or a hard mute with a 4 ms ramp)
interruptOpen.after: hard cut to the new format; its first frame is already in motion
interruptOpen.use: cliche setup (stiff announcement, stock intro) -> hard stop sound + freeze -> the real format; break the expectation inside 8 s (success-patterns.md 1, interrupted cliche)

verbLadder.use: one-word chapter verbs (Build. Expand. Automate. Multiply.), one beat each, the last one lands and holds; sparse VO or on-screen type

mockumentaryReaction.audio: L-split: the interview's room tone runs under each reaction insert (split.L)
mockumentaryReaction.use: documentary-parody comedy: interview line -> 0.3-0.5 s reaction insert -> back; the payoff line gets a beat of silence before it, a deadpan hold after it and the stinger on the cut out

sentenceLed.use: small type builds word by word on the beat grid, the full sentence holds, then the result shot cuts in on the next bar line (sentence-led product film)

lateDrop.pre_bed: UI ticks and texture only before the drop: no kick, no bass, no melody
lateDrop.drop_on: the first frame of the turn line or the product name
lateDrop.use: the problem plays near-silent on UI ticks for 10-60% of the runtime, an optional 0.5-1 s speech gap, then the beat drops exactly on the turn line or product name (round-3 tier A: 2 pieces, 6 in all)

preStingSilence.picture: the lockup holds still through the silence (no new motion); the sting cuts to a giant cropped mark or the end card
preStingSilence.use: end rule: after the lockup, 1-3 s of near-silence (bed out, room tone at most), then one final sting; an end-of-film device, not the 200 ms smash gag (cuts smash)

voiceHandoff.label: AI voice
voiceHandoff.label_rule: on screen in every frame where the synthetic voice speaks
requires: the honesty label on screen while it speaks
voiceHandoff.use: the presenter starts a line to camera, the synthetic voice carries it on while the presenter leaves frame; the caption speaker tag flips on the handoff frame; a live demo follows as the spine

steps.part: ui.checklist (a file chip: ui.fileChip is not built yet)

pipelineReveal.use: AI-builder launch: prompt -> agent plan -> render passes -> exploded / knolled -> file chip -> the product used in the world -> title; the music breaks down before the world shot and drops back on it

diagramWalkthrough.caption: the current sentence in a bar under the diagram
diagramWalkthrough.picture: one diagram, no cuts: it advances ONLY in the speech gaps; the camera re-frames the active region inside the same gap
diagramWalkthrough.use: VO explainer: one sentence per diagram step, the advance lands on gap start + 2 frames, the end card holds 3-8 s on near-silence (round-4/5 tier A reference: 14 gaps of 0.3-0.5 s, one about every 4 s)

queryLadder.use: one UI repeated over 4-6 rungs of escalating input (simple -> hard / other modality / other language), one VO line per rung, hardest rung last, then a pull back to where it runs with 2-3 benefit chips, then the repo or URL (round-4 tier A reference: 1.66% bookmarks)

fidelityLadder.use: the same output re-done at a higher quality or parameter, one step per bar with a live readout, a 2-3 s dropout (bed >= 20 dB under the body), then the result in a new dimension or format on the next downbeat, then the title (round-4 tier A reference: one step per bar at 99 BPM)

voicesColdOpen.rule: each montage window starts and ends mid-sentence on word boundaries; audio leads every picture cut (J); no names until the lead; each later super adds one personal detail
voicesColdOpen.use: documentary opener: 4-6 faces in 0.5-1.3 s cuts, each mid-sentence, then the lead's first full line with a name super at about 5-6 s (round-4 tier A reference: 5 faces in 5 s)

commandRapidFire.rule: each response lands on the frame after the command's last word ends (word_end frame + 1); hard cuts, no transitions between states
commandRapidFire.use: voice-first demo: a burst of short spoken commands, each answered by a UI change on the next frame, optional silent comic beats in the setup, close on a reaction beat (round-4 tier A* reference, claim-driven: about 16 commands in 17 s)

anaphoraCut.use: cut on each repetition of a spoken word or phrase ('here, here, here'; 'you are paying the X / the Y / the Z'): one shot or one slot word per repetition, so a spoken list becomes a montage (round-5 references: one reach-by-account-size, one boosted-looking, one tier A)

trailerArc.use: trailer: quiet dialogue (dips to black between lines) -> interstitial title cards (small line over large line) -> build -> sustained wall montage (about 1 cut/s) -> ONE question line over near-silence (2-4 s, bed >= 30 dB down) -> crescendo -> title -> hard stop -> date card -> sting (one reach-by-account-size reference; one tier A reference has the valley and the build)

styleLadder.renderer: hold ONE composition; swap the grade / stylize layer on the planned frames (layers look.*, transitions/sketchToRender for the sketch -> render step)
styleLadder.use: show a model's range in about 3 s: one held composition steps through render styles on hits (live -> toon 3D -> pencil -> watercolour, or any list of looks), 0.5-1 s each (tier C reference: craft only)

defaults.sentence: Launch day breaks the same thing:
value: Your plan stays in one place

problemPivot.use: a CONTINUOUS typographic film (zero cuts, synced by motion events): a sentence typed with an accent-word punchline, a three-beat problem ladder (2-2.5 s a beat, the diagram worse each beat), a 1.5-2 s audio gap (the bed thins to a hum, then true silence; plan.audio.quiet kind gap) that starts inside the last beat and ends ON the pivot frame, where colour, bass and the brand line arrive together (a sub hit on the frame, the bed back on it, the ribbon and colour a few frames after), a three-beat value ladder, a typed command CTA with the address, and a quiet hold of at least 2 s (kind hold). One tier-B reference (an inference from its like rate; nothing shows reach was paid for), treated as craft (docs/research/reference-round6-2026-10.md)

picture.chip: a persistent corner chip flips its label, icon and colour on the flip frame (flash, then tick)
picture.wipe: a wipe edge crosses the shot and the audio switches on the frame the edge is at the centre
picture.slider: a round-handled line sweeps across the live shot; the audio switches on the frame the handle crosses the centre, and the overlay text is wiped by the same line

abReplay.use: the before / after audio swap: one clip is heard twice (stem A, then stem B) and the swap lands on the SAME frame as the picture flip (a chip, a wipe or a slider); the halves are level-matched within 1 dB so the difference reads as content, not loudness; in replay mode the picture is frame-identical across the two passes; numbers are house starting values from two tier-A reference posts (flip at about 40-45 % of the runtime, halves matched within 1 dB) and are tunable (docs/research/reference-mirelo-2026-10.md)

onset_snap.note: studied launch and motion films put 45-80% of their cuts within 2 frames of a sound onset (success-patterns.md 4); the 60% target is for music-led, cut-driven pieces only (VO-led and continuous films are scored by their mode, references/critic.md); cutgen.py snap moves each cut to the nearest onset within the tolerance

accelerate3Act.use: trailer montage: act 1 holds (the world), act 2 halves the shot length (the turn), act 3 runs 2 beats -> 1 beat -> 8th notes (the wall); every cut on a half-beat of the score, a braam on act-2 every-other and act-3 every bar downbeat; templates/trailer and cuts/trailer_plan.py

hitSilenceHit.use: the last wall hit, the picture cuts to black on the next frame, 1-3 s of planned silence (a faint ring at most), then the title hit; mark the silence in plan.audio.quiet (kind gap)

silenceBeforeHit.bed: digital silence (horror) or a sub 38-40 dB under the wall
silenceBeforeHit.picture: black, or one held frame with one line of dialogue
silenceBeforeHit.use: the stop: the wall cuts on a downbeat, a reverse suck ends on the stop frame, then nothing; the title lands on the next downbeat

cutdown30.use: the 30 s cut-down of the same plan: no world beat, a 1-bar production card, shorter acts, the same title hit

cutdown15.use: the 15 s cut-down: a cold-open image, one wall bar run, the silence, the title, the date
